    The kernel follows the mathematical definition:
        out[n, c_out, h_out, w_out] =
            sum_{c_in, k_h, k_w}
                in[n, c_in, h_in, w_in] *
                weight[c_in, c_out, K-1-k_h, K-1-k_w]

    where
        h_in = (h_out + padding - k_h) // stride  (if divisible)
        w_in = (w_out + padding - k_w) // stride  (if divisible)
    """

    P = padding
    OP = out_pad

    def conv_transpose2d_fp16(
        A: T.Buffer[(T.int64(), T.int64(), T.int64(), T.int64()), "float16"],   # (N, C_in, H, W)
        Wg: T.Buffer[(T.int64(), T.int64(), T.int64(), T.int64()), "float16"],  # (C_in, C_out, K, K)
        O: T.Buffer[(T.int64(), T.int64(), T.int64(), T.int64()), "float16"]    # (N, C_out, H_out, W_out)

        C_IN = T.int64()
        H = T.int64()
        W = T.int64()
        C_OUT = T.int64()
        K = T.int64()

        W_OUT = (W - 1) * S - 2 * P + K + OP

            for c_in, k_h, k_w in T.grid(C_IN, K, K):

                pw = w_out + P - k_w

                cond_w = pw % S == 0

    """
    Returns a list containing a single fp16 CUDA tensor matching the
    reference test case.
    """
    batch_size = 8
    in_channels = 64
    height = 1024
    width = 1024
    x = torch.rand(batch_size, in_channels, height, width,
                   dtype=torch.float16, device="cuda")
    return [x]

def get_init_inputs():
    """
    Provides the arguments required to construct ModelNew.
    """
    in_channels = 64
    out_channels = 64
    kernel_size = 3
    return [in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size]
